headline: Mayor Brenda Locke and Surrey Police Board Reach $284.5 Million Operational Budget Accord
summary: Surrey Mayor Brenda Locke finalizes a $284.5 million municipal policing agreement with the Surrey Police Board, capping property tax impacts while maintaining frontline transition targets.
body:
SURREY, BC — Surrey Mayor Brenda Locke and the Surrey Police Board finalized a landmark $284.5 million operational budget agreement, establishing financial certainty for the ongoing municipal transition to the Surrey Police Service (SPS).

## Budget Compromise and Fiscal Discipline

The agreement resolves months of intergovernmental deliberations after Mayor Locke firmly rejected an earlier $91 million budget increase request that would have triggered an estimated 18% municipal property tax increase for Surrey homeowners. The finalized framework incorporates approximately $40 million in unspent operational reserves from the prior fiscal cycle.

Mayor Locke emphasized that the negotiated figure protects local ratepayers while fulfilling statutory public safety requirements established by the Ministry of Public Safety and Solicitor General.

## Council Deliberations and Party Positions

Surrey Connect councillors supported the agreement as a demonstration of responsible fiscal management, while Surrey First and Safe Surrey Coalition members questioned long-term capital forecasting.

The Surrey Police Union noted that stable funding allocations provide hiring predictability for frontline officer deployment across Guildford, Newton, and South Surrey precincts.

## Next Implementation and Oversight Steps

The City of Surrey Finance Committee will receive quarterly expenditure audits from the Police Board throughout the fiscal year.

headline: Councillor Linda Annis Unveils 300-Officer Public Safety Plan and Police Training Academy Proposal
summary: Surrey First Councillor Linda Annis introduces a municipal public safety strategy proposing 300 additional officers over four years and a municipal police training center.
body:
SURREY, BC — Surrey City Councillor Linda Annis (Surrey First) presented a comprehensive municipal public safety framework at Surrey City Hall, calling for the staged recruitment of 300 additional police officers over the next four years.

## 300-Officer Recruitment and Municipal Training Academy

Under Councillor Annis's proposal, the City of Surrey would onboard 75 frontline officers annually while establishing a state-of-the-art regional police training academy in Cloverdale. The initiative also earmarks funding for 600 high-definition intersection cameras connected directly to emergency dispatch operations.

Councillor Annis stated that with Surrey rapidly approaching a population of 700,000, frontline staffing ratios must keep pace with rapid urban growth and commercial expansion in City Centre and South Surrey.

## Fiscal Modeling and Council Debate

The Surrey First caucus proposed funding the safety expansion by reallocating capital reserves from discretionary civic projects, such as the proposed 10,000-seat entertainment arena, directly toward neighborhood policing hubs.

Council members debated the impact of debt-servicing costs on the city's 10-year capital plan.

## Public Consultation and Committee Review

The public safety framework will be referred to the Surrey Public Safety Advisory Committee for stakeholder review.

headline: Councillors Doug Elford and Mandeep Nagra Demand 60-Day Permit Approvals Under Surrey 2050 Plan
summary: Safe Surrey Coalition Councillors Doug Elford and Mandeep Nagra advocate for expedited 60-day residential building permits and zero property tax increases during official community plan debates.
body:
SURREY, BC — Surrey City Councillors Doug Elford and Mandeep Nagra (Safe Surrey Coalition) voiced strong support for streamlining municipal residential construction approvals during deliberations on the draft Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan (OCP).

## Expedited Building Permits and Transit Corridor Density

Councillors Elford and Nagra proposed a binding municipal service guarantee requiring staff to process multi-family residential building permits within 60 days along the upcoming Surrey-Langley SkyTrain extension corridor. They argued that administrative delays in the planning department have stalled affordable rental housing starts.

Councillor Elford underscored that rapid housing delivery near future rapid transit stations in Fleetwood and Clayton is vital to maintaining affordability for young families and seniors.

## Fiscal Policy and Tax Freeze Commitments

Both councillors advocated for a multi-year municipal property tax freeze, urging council to offset revenue gaps by capturing development cost charges from booming transit-oriented developments.

Surrey Connect majority members expressed caution regarding the fiscal viability of municipal tax freezes given rising regional infrastructure costs.

## Next Legislative Phase

The Surrey Planning and Development Department will submit final revisions to the Surrey 2050 OCP in October.

headline: Councillor Mike Bose Leads Surrey Council Initiative to Protect Farmland and Expand Food Hubs
summary: Surrey First Councillor Mike Bose spearheads agricultural preservation guidelines, safeguarding farmland in Serpentine and Nicomekl valleys while advancing municipal food security hubs.
body:
SURREY, BC — Surrey City Councillor Mike Bose (Surrey First) introduced a motion before Surrey City Council directing staff to strengthen municipal buffers protecting agricultural lands from encroaching industrial and commercial developments.

## Farmland Preservation in Serpentine-Nicomekl Valleys

Councillor Bose, a fourth-generation Surrey farmer and long-time agricultural advocate, emphasized that Surrey's 19,000 acres of fertile farmland in the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) represent a critical regional food security asset that must not be compromised for speculative warehousing projects.

The approved policy directive mandates enhanced drainage infrastructure investments and updated dyking systems across the Serpentine and Nicomekl floodplains to protect active vegetable and dairy farms from extreme weather events.

## Surrey Agri-Food Innovation Network

Councillor Bose also proposed expanding municipal partnerships with Kwantlen Polytechnic University’s School of Horticulture to build local food aggregation and processing hubs in Cloverdale.

Council voted unanimously in favor of supporting drainage maintenance grants for local agricultural producers.

## Implementation Roadmap

City engineering staff will table the Agriculture Drainage Master Plan before the Environment Committee next quarter.

headline: Councillor Gordon Hepner Advances $45 Million Parkland and Community Sports Infrastructure Expansion
summary: Parks and Recreation Committee Chair Gordon Hepner guides council approval of $45 million in new athletic fields, turf upgrades, and neighborhood park acquisitions across Surrey.
body:
SURREY, BC — Surrey City Councillor Gordon Hepner (Surrey Connect), serving as Chair of the Parks, Recreation and Sport Tourism Committee, announced council approval for a $45 million sports park infrastructure development program.

## Community Athletic Facilities and Neighborhood Parks

The capital package includes the construction of three new all-weather synthetic turf soccer and rugby pitches at Cloverdale Athletic Park, expanded lighting at Newton Athletic Park, and the acquisition of five acres of parkland in fast-growing Grandview Heights in South Surrey.

Councillor Hepner highlighted that with thousands of youth participating in organized sports leagues across Surrey, modernizing field capacity ensures equitable access for grassroots community athletics.

## Funding Structure and Development Cost Allocations

The parkland acquisitions are financed through Developer Cost Charges (DCCs) levied on new residential developments, minimizing the direct burden on the general municipal operating tax base.

Local minor sports associations welcomed the expanded field hours and LED energy-efficient lighting upgrades.

## Construction Timeline

Groundbreaking on the Cloverdale synthetic turf expansion is scheduled for September 2026, with completion expected by spring 2027.

headline: Councillor Pardeep Kooner Leads Surrey Initiative to Fast-Track Urgent and Primary Healthcare Clinics
summary: Environment and Community Services Committee Chair Pardeep Kooner sponsors policy streamlining municipal permits for urgent primary healthcare centers in underserved neighborhoods.
body:
SURREY, BC — Surrey City Councillor Pardeep Kooner (Surrey Connect) brought forward an initiative to expedite municipal development permits and provide zoning waivers for primary care clinics and urgent medical centers.

## Municipal Support for Primary Healthcare Access

Recognizing severe patient backlogs at Surrey Memorial Hospital's emergency department, Councillor Kooner’s motion directs city staff to create an expedited 'Priority Healthcare Permit Queue' for medical practitioners establishing family practices, pediatric clinics, and urgent care hubs in Surrey.

Councillor Kooner stated that while healthcare delivery is primarily a provincial mandate, municipal government must remove bureaucratic red tape that delays doctors from opening community clinics in Guildford, Newton, and Fleetwood.

## Intergovernmental Collaboration with Fraser Health

The policy directs city administration to coordinate directly with Fraser Health Authority and local divisions of family practice to identify priority locations near public transit lines.

Local medical associations commended Surrey City Council for taking proactive municipal steps to attract healthcare professionals.

## Implementation Guidelines

The expedited healthcare permitting framework takes effect across Surrey planning offices immediately.

headline: Public Safety Chair Rob Stutt Advances Automated Speed Enforcement and Real-Time Camera Access
summary: Surrey Public Safety Committee Chair Rob Stutt oversees municipal camera integration and school zone safety enforcement to reduce pedestrian traffic incidents.
body:
SURREY, BC — Surrey City Councillor Rob Stutt (Surrey Connect), serving as Chair of the Public Safety Committee, presented an updated traffic safety and automated monitoring framework to Surrey City Council.

## Traffic Safety Technology and School Zone Enforcement

Councillor Stutt, a former veteran police investigator, guided the approval of enhanced speed-monitoring radar displays and upgraded high-definition traffic camera integrations across 40 high-risk school zones and arterial intersections in Surrey.

Councillor Stutt emphasized that leveraging modern automated traffic management technology allows police officers to focus on criminal investigations and extortion suppression while significantly improving road safety for students and pedestrians.

## Inter-Agency Coordination

The initiative establishes a secure data-sharing protocol between the City of Surrey Traffic Management Centre and law enforcement agencies to accelerate hit-and-run and collision investigations.

Parent Advisory Councils across Surrey School District 36 expressed strong support for increased automated enforcement in school zones.

## Rollout Horizon

The automated camera installations will be completed prior to the opening of the school year in September 2026.

headline: Councillor Harry Bains Leads Surrey Small Business Commercial Permitting Modernization
summary: Surrey City Councillor Harry Bains shepherds council approval for streamlined commercial licensing, cutting red tape for neighborhood retail, restaurants, and tech startups.
body:
SURREY, BC — Surrey City Councillor Harry Bains (Surrey Connect) secured unanimous council support for the 'Surrey Business First' regulatory reform package, modernizing commercial tenant improvement permitting across the city.

## Commercial Licensing Reform and Red Tape Reduction

Councillor Bains, an entrepreneur and civic advocate, stated that simplifying business license renewals and establishing digital fast-track processing for restaurant and retail tenant improvements will stimulate private investment in Newton and Cloverdale town centres.

The reform eliminates redundant building inspections for low-risk commercial alterations and introduces an online portal that reduces commercial permit wait times from months to under ten business days.

## Economic Development and Small Business Advocacy

The Surrey Board of Trade and local Business Improvement Associations (BIAs) endorsed the initiative, noting that streamlined municipal approvals lower startup capital barriers for new entrepreneurs.

Councillor Bains reaffirmed council's commitment to fostering a diversified local economy that supports family-owned enterprises alongside high-tech development in City Centre.

## Digital Portal Launch

The digital commercial licensing portal will go live on the city website on August 15, 2026.
